pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Wyoming electrician licensing is administered through the Wyoming Department of Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety. The state licenses electrical workers at the journeyman and master levels, and candidates must follow the current Wyoming electrical licensing process before receiving a journeyman electrician license. The Wyoming Journeyman Electrician exam is commonly listed as the Wyoming 385 Journeyman Electrician examination. The exam is open book and includes 80 questions with a 4-hour time allowance. Candidates must earn a passing score of 70%. The exam is based on the National Electrical Code edition adopted for Wyoming electrical testing and includes questions related to trade knowledge and electrical code application. Major journeyman electrician exam categories include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Wyoming uses a state-level electrical licensing structure through the Wyoming Department of Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety. The state regulates electrician licensing, electrical installations, inspections, and electrical safety requirements. Candidates preparing for a Wyoming Master Electrician license should follow the state licensing process rather than a local-only license path. Candidates pursuing this credential should be ready to demonstrate strong technical knowledge, code understanding, calculation ability, safety awareness, and knowledge of the responsibilities that come with advanced electrical licensing. Electrical licensing involves more than field installation work. It includes responsibility for code-compliant work, safe electrical installations, supervision, inspection readiness, customer obligations, contractor-related responsibilities, licensing compliance, renewal, and state rules.
